identity.title: Independent Core Rotation in Massive Filaments in Orion

question.value: Are the rotation axes of dense cores in OMC-2/OMC-3 aligned with their host filaments, and how much angular momentum and rotational support do the cores have?

evidence.quote: In this work, we focus on the angular momentum of cores and its relation with respect to filaments.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00662.S.
We mapped OMC-2 and OMC-3 in N$_{2}$H$^{+}$ (1–0) with ALMA in November 2014 and August 2015 in band 3.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 35 kHz channel width, 0.11 km/s at 93 GHz

evidence.quote: The frequency resolution of N$_{2}$H$^{+}$ is 35 kHz, which corresponds to a velocity resolution of 0.11 km$\,s^{-1}\,$ at 93 GHz.
which corresponds to a velocity resolution of 0.11 km$\,s^{-1}\,$ at 93 GHz

arrays.value: 12-m main array and ACA; mosaics of 11 pointings (OMC-3) and 7 pointings (OMC-2)

evidence.quote: We used the 12-m main array and the Atacama Compact Array (ACA) to mosaic OMC-3 with 11 pointings, and OMC-2 with 7 pointings.
The baselines of the 12-m main array and the ACA observations are at a range of 13.6 – 340.0 m and 6.8 – 87.4 m, respectively.
The N$_{2}$H$^{+}$ (1–0) images have an angular resolution of $\sim$ 3$^{"}$
with ALMA in November 2014 and August 2015 in band 3

provided.value: Single-dish N2H+ (1-0) data combined with ALMA to recover missing flux

evidence.quote: The single dish data of N$_{2}$H$^{+}$ (1–0) were taken from the NRO (Nobeyama Radio Observatory) Star Formation Legacy Project (cite: nakamura2019).
The values of Mass and Mass$_{vir}$ are from (cite: lid2013).
Major and Minor axes are from (cite: nutter2007).

array_combination.value: ALMA (12m+ACA) combined with Nobeyama single-dish in CASA

evidence.quote: The combination was performed using CASA (Common Astronomy Software Applications) (cite: mcmullin2007).

what.value: Filament orientation fitting via autocorrelation function

evidence.quote: fit them following the procedures described in (cite: lihb2013)
measure the velocity gradients following the method described in (cite: goodman1993)
The details of the Monte Carlo simulations can be found in Appendix A of (cite: stephens2017).

method.value: Combined interferometric and single-dish N2H+ cubes in CASA to recover missing flux

evidence.quote: We combined the N$_{2}$H$^{+}$ data from ALMA and Nobeyama to recover missing fluxes in the interferometric data.

method.value: Autocorrelation of integrated intensity map via FFT; least-squares long-axis fit to the contour at 20% of peak

evidence.quote: For a given contour of this autocorrelation map, the long axis direction ($\theta_{f}$) can be obtained by performing a least-squares fit to the pixel positions located within the contour.
In subsequent calculations, the contour at 20% of the peak value was adopted.

validation.value: Variation of < 5 deg among contour levels

evidence.quote: only $< 5^{\circ}$ variation was found among different trials

method.value: Single Gaussian fit to the isolated hyperfine component, then planar fit v_LSR = v0 + a dα + b dδ

evidence.quote: We then fit the velocity field as $v_{LSR} = v_0 + a \Delta \alpha + b \Delta \delta$

key_parameters.value: Require peak > 3 rms and fitting errors

evidence.quote: we require the spectral lines to have peak intensity greater than three times of the Root Mean Square (rms) noise
We adopt a distance of 400 pc for OMC-2 and OMC-3

validation.value: Single-Gaussian fit compared with fitting all hyperfine components; no significant difference

evidence.quote: we compared fitting all hyperfine components and fitting just the isolated one with a single Gaussian. No significant difference was found.

analysis_steps.goal: test alignment of rotation and filaments

method.value: Compare |θf−θG| with 3D random-vector Monte Carlo projected to 2D using an Anderson-Darling test

evidence.quote: 10$^{6}$ pairs of unit vectors are generated to produce 10$^{6}$ angles of $\theta_{3D}$
the AD test gives a $p$–value of 0.97, consistent of being random

method.value: J/M = 0.59 G R^2 and beta = 0.34 G^2 R^3/(GM)

evidence.quote: cores have a power-law profile density ($\rho \propto R^{-1.6}$)

validation.value: Slope compared with 1.6 from Goodman et al. 1993

evidence.quote: The slope is consistent with the index value of 1.6 found by  (cite: goodman1993)
The combination was performed using CASA (Common Astronomy Software Applications) (cite: mcmullin2007).
The measured 2D velocity gradients of cores are between 1.3 and 16.7 km s$^{-1}$ pc$^{-1}$
specific angular momentum ($J/M$) between 0.0012 and 0.016 pc km s$^{-1}$
ranges from 0.00041 to 0.094

results_numeric.quantity: AD test p-value vs random distribution

evidence.quote: the AD test gives a $p$–value of 0.97
the gradient directions of 7 cores ($\sim$23%) are essentially parallel to their filament orientations
the gradient directions of 8 cores ($\sim$27%) are essentially perpendicular to their filaments

findings_qualitative.value: Rotation provides insignificant support against gravitational collapse (small beta).

evidence.quote: these small values of $\beta$ indicate that rotation alone is not enough to support the core from collapsing due to gravity

claims.hypothesis: Core rotation axes are correlated with host filament elongation
claims.experiment: Compared |θf−θG| for 30 cores with a 3D random Monte Carlo distribution using an AD test
claims.finding: Core rotation axes are independent of the filament orientation

evidence.quote: the cores’ rotational axes have no discernible correlation with the elongation of their hosting filament

claims.hypothesis: Specific angular momentum scales with core size
claims.experiment: Computed J/M from gradients and fitted a power law vs R
claims.finding: Consistent with the index 1.6 of Goodman et al. 1993

evidence.quote: We find that $J/M$ increases with increasing $R$, following a power-law $J/M~\propto~R^{1.52~\pm~0.14}$.

claims.experiment: Computed beta, the ratio of rotational to gravitational energy
claims.finding: Rotation is insufficient to prevent collapse

evidence.quote: indicating that rotation cannot stop gravitational collapse in these dense cores

why_this_data.value: N2H+ (1-0) traces cold dense gas and ALMA resolution reaches the thermal Jeans scale

evidence.quote: making N$_{2}$H$^{+}$ (1–0) especially suitable for tracing dense cores and filaments

limitations_admitted.value: Differences in methods and samples among studies; a much larger sample is needed to tackle the issue systematically.

evidence.quote: high spectral and spatial images of a much larger sample are needed to tackle the issue systematically

referee_caveats_inferred: Only 2D projected angles with a coarse 3D random model; the p-value of 0.97 with N=30 has limited power
Single-Gaussian fits and gradient direction can be affected by outflows and infall
Core sizes and masses are taken from other works with different resolution
The beta and J/M uncertainties are dominated by the density profile assumption
